title: How El Niño reaches Sri Lanka's rain

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: In late 2026, the sea along the equator in the Pacific ran about two degrees warmer than normal. That's El Niño.

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: That's the other side of the world. Does Sri Lanka even feel it?

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: We checked {{n_years|word}} years of satellite rain records for Sri Lanka.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: In {{ond_wet_vs_neutral_n}} of {{n_nino}} El Niño years, October to December was wetter than a typical year with no El Niño or La Niña.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: The January to March after? Drier on average, but less reliably.

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: So an El Niño year means a wet end of the year?

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: It has leaned that way, but in {{ond_dry_vs_neutral_n|word}} El Niño years it didn't. For your area, follow the Department of Meteorology.

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: Warm water far away, a nudge to the rain right here.
